modern: O Lord, you have made a covenant with me, your servant, in Christ Jesus my Lord; and now, I beg you, let my children be included in its gracious provisions. Let me believe this promise as made to me as well as to Abraham. I know that my children are born in sin and shaped in wickedness, just like other people’s; so I ask nothing on the ground of their birth, for I know well that “that which is born of the flesh is flesh,” and nothing more. Lord, make them to be born under your covenant of grace by your Holy Spirit!

I pray for my descendants through all generations. Be their God as you are mine. My highest honor is that you have let me serve you; may my children serve you in all the years to come. O God of Abraham, be the God of his Isaac! O God of Hannah, accept her Samuel!

If, Lord, you have blessed me in my family, I pray you to remember other households of your people that are still unblessed. Be the God of all the families of Israel. Don’t let a single one of those who fear your name be tried with a godless and wicked household, for your Son Jesus Christ’s sake. Amen.

notes.note: Offspring, descendants.
Beg.
“Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me” ([[Ps.51.5|Psalm 51:5]]).

notes.term: That which is born of the flesh is flesh
notes.note: Jesus to Nicodemus ([[John.3.6|John 3:6]]).
God’s binding promise to save his people through Christ, freely, as a gift and not a reward.

notes.term: O God of Hannah, accept her Samuel
notes.note: Hannah gave the son she had prayed for back to the Lord: “as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the LORD” ([[1Sam.1.27-1Sam.1.28|1 Samuel 1:27–28]]).

modern: Many a true servant of the Lord is slow of speech, and when he is called on to plead for his Lord, he is in great confusion for fear he will spoil a good cause by arguing it badly. In such a case it is good to remember that the Lord made the tongue that is so slow, and we must take care not to blame our Maker. It may be that a slow tongue isn’t as great an evil as a fast one, and that few words may be more of a blessing than floods of wordiness. It is also quite certain that real saving power doesn’t lie in human rhetoric, with its figures of speech, its pretty phrases and its grand displays. Lack of fluency isn’t as great a lack as it looks.

If God is with our mouth and with our mind, we will have something better than the sounding brass of eloquence or the tinkling cymbal of persuasion. God’s teaching is wisdom; his presence is power. Pharaoh had more reason to fear stammering Moses than the most fluent talker in Egypt, for what he said had power in it: he spoke plagues and deaths. If the Lord is with us in our natural weakness, we will be clothed with supernatural power. So let’s speak for Jesus boldly, as we ought to speak.

notes.term: I will be with thy mouth
notes.note: God’s answer when Moses said he was “slow of speech”: “Who hath made man’s mouth?” ([[Exod.4.10-Exod.4.12|Exodus 4:10–12]]).
Pleading someone’s case.
Wordiness; too many words.
Figures of speech.

notes.term: The sounding brass… the tinkling cymbal
notes.note: “Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal” ([[1Cor.13.1|1 Corinthians 13:1]]).
Belted, clothed.

notes.term: Speak for Jesus boldly, as we ought to speak
notes.note: “That therein I may speak boldly, as I ought to speak” ([[Eph.6.20|Ephesians 6:20]]).

modern: Strangers, temporary residents and hired servants weren’t allowed to eat the holy things. It is still so in spiritual matters. But two kinds of people were free to eat at the sacred table: those bought with the priest’s money, and those born in the priest’s house. Bought and born: these were the two undeniable proofs of a right to holy things.

Bought. Our great High Priest has bought with a price all those who put their trust in him. They are his absolute property, entirely the Lord’s. Not for what they are in themselves, but for their owner’s sake, they are admitted to the same privileges he himself enjoys, and “they shall eat of his meat.” He has food to eat that the worldly know nothing about. “Because ye belong to Christ,” you will therefore share with your Lord.

Born. This is an equally sure way to privilege. If we are born in the Priest’s house, we take our place with the rest of the family. Regeneration makes us fellow heirs and members of the same body; and so the peace, the joy, the glory the Father has given to Christ, Christ has given to us. Redemption and regeneration have given us a double claim to the divine permission in this promise.

notes.term: They shall eat of his meat
notes.note: Only the priest’s household could eat the holy food from the offerings ([[Lev.22.10-Lev.22.11|Leviticus 22:10–11]]). Meat means food.
Foreigners living somewhere for a while.
“For ye are bought with a price” ([[1Cor.6.20|1 Corinthians 6:20]]).

notes.term: Meat to eat which worldlings know not of
notes.note: “I have meat to eat that ye know not of” ([[John.4.32|John 4:32]]). Worldlings are people who live only for this world.
Being born again: the new life God gives by his Spirit.

notes.term: Fellow-heirs, and of the same body
notes.note: [[Eph.3.6|Ephesians 3:6]].

modern: This first clause of the high priest’s blessing is in substance a promise. The blessing our great High Priest pronounces on us is sure to come, for he speaks the mind of God.

What a joy to live under the divine blessing! It puts a gracious flavor into everything. If we are blessed, then all our possessions and pleasures are blessed; yes, our losses and crosses, and even our disappointments, are blessed. God’s blessing is deep, emphatic, effective. A man’s blessing may begin and end in words; but the blessing of the Lord makes rich and makes holy. The best wish we can have for our dearest friend isn’t “May prosperity attend thee,” but “The Lord bless thee.”

It is just as delightful to be kept by God: kept by him, kept near him, kept in him. They are kept indeed whom God keeps; they are guarded from evil and reserved for boundless happiness. God’s keeping goes with his blessing, to establish it and make it last.

The author of this little book wishes that the rich blessing and sure keeping pronounced here may come on every reader who is looking at these lines right now. Please breathe the text to God as a prayer for his servants.

notes.term: The Lord bless thee, and keep thee
notes.note: The opening of the blessing God gave Aaron and his sons to pronounce over Israel ([[Num.6.24-Num.6.26|Numbers 6:24–26]]).
A blessing.
Effective; actually doing what it sets out to do.

notes.term: The blessing of the Lord makes rich
notes.note: “The blessing of the LORD, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it” ([[Prov.10.22|Proverbs 10:22]]).
“Reserved in heaven for you, who are kept by the power of God” ([[1Pet.1.4-1Pet.1.5|1 Peter 1:4–5]]).

modern: Put the law into the heart, and the whole person is right. This is where the law belongs, for there it lies, like the tablets of stone in the ark, in the place appointed for it. In the head it puzzles, on the back it burdens, in the heart it holds us up.

What a choice phrase is used here: “the law of his God”! When we know the Lord as our own God, his law becomes freedom to us. God with us in covenant makes us eager to obey his will and walk in his commands. Is the command my Father’s command? Then I delight in it.

We are guaranteed here that the man with an obedient heart will be held up in every step he takes. He will do what is right, and so he will do what is wise. Holy action is always the most sensible, though at the time it may not seem so. We are moving along the great highway of God’s providence and grace when we keep to the way of his law. The Word of God has never misled a single soul yet. Its plain directions to walk humbly, justly, lovingly and in the fear of the Lord are as much words of wisdom to make our way prosperous as rules of holiness to keep our garments clean. He walks surely who walks righteously.

notes.term: Like the tables of stone in the ark
notes.note: Moses put the tablets of the law inside the ark of the covenant ([[Deut.10.5|Deuteronomy 10:5]]).
Freedom. “And I will walk at liberty: for I seek thy precepts” ([[Ps.119.45|Psalm 119:45]]).
A command.
Sensible, wise.
God’s care and control over everything that happens, providing for his people.
“Blessed is he that watcheth, and keepeth his garments” ([[Rev.16.15|Revelation 16:15]]).

notes.term: He walks surely who walks righteously
notes.note: “He that walketh uprightly walketh surely” ([[Prov.10.9|Proverbs 10:9]]).

modern: There is an inheritance of grace that we ought to be bold enough to win as our own possession. Everything one believer has gained is open to another. We can be strong in faith, fervent in love and abundant in work; there is nothing to stop it. Let’s go up and take possession. The sweetest experience and the brightest grace are as much for us as for any of our brothers and sisters. Jehovah has set it before us; no one can deny our right; let’s go up and possess it in his name.

The world too lies before us, to be conquered for the Lord Jesus. We aren’t to leave any country or corner of it unconquered. That slum near our house is set before us, not to defeat our efforts but to give way to them. We have only to summon enough courage to go forward, and we will win dark homes and hard hearts for Jesus. Let’s never leave the people in a lane or alley to die because we don’t have enough faith in Jesus and his gospel to go up and possess the land. No spot is too dark, no person too godless, to be beyond the power of grace. Cowardice, be gone! Faith marches to the conquest.

notes.note: Moses urging Israel to enter Canaan, which they then refused to do out of fear ([[Deut.1.21-Deut.1.26|Deuteronomy 1:21–26]]).
Inheritance.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
In spiritual darkness; ignorant.
Openly godless.

modern: Yes, the Lord will be with us in our holy war, but he requires us to follow his rules strictly. Our victories will depend very much on our obeying him with all our heart, throwing strength and courage into the actions of our faith. If we are halfhearted, we can’t expect more than half a blessing.

We must obey the Lord with care and thought. “Observe to do” is the phrase used, and it is full of meaning. This applies to every part of God’s will; we must obey with an all-round readiness. Our rule of conduct is “according to all the law.” We may not pick and choose; we must take the Lord’s commands as they come, one and all. In all this we must go on with exactness and steadiness. Ours is to be a straight course that bends neither to the right nor to the left. We aren’t to go wrong by being stricter than the law, or turn aside out of carelessness to a freer and easier way. With obedience like this, spiritual prosperity will come. O Lord, help us see whether it isn’t so! We won’t test your promise in vain.

notes.term: Be thou strong and very courageous
notes.note: God’s charge to Joshua as he took over from Moses ([[Josh.1.6-Josh.1.9|Joshua 1:6–9]]).
Take care to do.
Wherever.
Lightness; not taking something seriously.
Steadiness; faithfulness.

modern: In prophecy, these are the words of the Messiah in the day of his obedience to death, when he gave his back to those who struck him and his cheeks to those who pulled out his beard. He was confident of divine support, and he trusted in Jehovah.

O my soul, your sorrows are like the fine dust on the scales compared with your Lord’s! Can’t you believe that the Lord God will help you? Your Lord was in a unique position. As the representative of sinful men, their substitute and sacrifice, it was necessary for the Father to leave him and let him come under desertion of soul. No such necessity is laid on you; you aren’t bound to cry, “Why hast thou forsaken me?” Did your Savior go on relying on God even then, and can’t you? He died for you, and so made it impossible for you to be left alone; so take heart.

In today’s work or trials, say, “The Lord God will help me.” Go out boldly. Set your face like flint, and resolve that no faintness or shame will come near you. If God helps, who can hinder? If you are sure of almighty help, what can be too heavy for you? Begin the day joyfully, and let no shadow of doubt come between you and the eternal sunshine.

notes.term: The Lord God will help me
notes.note: [[Isa.50.7|Isaiah 50:7]], from Isaiah’s picture of the suffering Servant.

notes.term: He gave His back to the smiters
notes.note: “I gave my back to the smiters, and my cheeks to them that plucked off the hair” ([[Isa.50.6|Isaiah 50:6]]). Smiters are those who strike.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.

notes.term: The small dust of the balance
notes.note: “Behold, the nations are… counted as the small dust of the balance” ([[Isa.40.15|Isaiah 40:15]]): too slight to tip the scales.
Special, belonging particularly to someone (not odd).
Jesus’ cry from the cross ([[Matt.27.46|Matthew 27:46]]).
So, therefore.
All-powerful.

modern: This is a precious promise for anyone who lives to be fruitful. At first it seems to have a sharp look. Must the fruitful branch be pruned? Must the knife cut even the best and most useful? No doubt it must, for a great deal of our Lord’s pruning is done by means of afflictions of one kind or another. It isn’t the evil but the good who are promised tribulation in this life. But then the end more than makes up for the painful means. If we can bear more fruit for our Lord, we won’t mind the pruning and the loss of leaves.

Still, pruning is sometimes done by the Word, apart from trial, and this takes away whatever seemed harsh in the taste of the promise. By the Word we will be made more gracious and more useful. The Lord, who has made us fruitful to some extent, will work on us until we reach a far higher degree of fruitfulness. Isn’t this a great joy? Truly there is more comfort in a promise of fruitfulness than if we had been guaranteed riches, or health, or honor.
Lord Jesus, quickly fulfill your gracious word to me, and make me abound in fruit to your praise!

notes.note: Prunes; cleans. “I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman” ([[John.15.1-John.15.2|John 15:1–2]]).
Trouble, suffering.
“In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world” ([[John.16.33|John 16:33]]).
Compensation; making up for something.
Worked.

notes.term: Purging is sometimes wrought by the Word
notes.note: “Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you” ([[John.15.3|John 15:3]]).
Guaranteed.

modern: All my changes come from him who never changes. If I had grown rich, I would have seen his hand in it and praised him; let me just as clearly see his hand if I am made poor, and praise him just as heartily. When we go down in the world, it is from the Lord, and so we can take it patiently; when we rise in the world, it is from the Lord, and we can accept it thankfully. Either way, the Lord has done it, and it is well.

It seems to be Jehovah’s way to lower those he means to raise, and to strip those he intends to clothe. If it is his way, it is the wisest and best way. If I am now going through the bringing low, I may well rejoice, because I see in it the prelude to the lifting up. The more we are humbled by grace, the more we will be exalted in glory. The poverty that will be turned to our enrichment is to be welcomed.

O Lord, you have taken me down lately and made me feel my insignificance and sin. It isn’t a pleasant experience, but I pray you to make it a profitable one for me. Oh, that you would fit me like this to bear a greater weight of delight and usefulness; and when I am ready for it, then give it to me, for Christ’s sake! Amen.

notes.term: The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich
notes.note: From Hannah’s song after the birth of Samuel ([[1Sam.2.7-1Sam.2.8|1 Samuel 2:7–8]]).
“For I am the LORD, I change not” ([[Mal.3.6|Malachi 3:6]]).
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
Turned by God’s control to a good end.
“He that humbleth himself shall be exalted” ([[Luke.14.11|Luke 14:11]]).

modern: Blessed posture: waiting truly, and only, on the Lord! May this be our condition all today and every day: waiting for his time, waiting in his service, waiting in joyful expectation, waiting in prayer and contentment. When the very soul waits like this, it is in the best and truest condition of a creature before his Creator, a servant before his Master, a child before his Father. We allow ourselves no dictating to God and no complaining about him; we will permit no sulking and no distrust. At the same time, we don’t run ahead of the cloud or look to others for help; neither of those would be waiting on God. God, and God alone, is what our hearts are waiting for.

Blessed assurance: salvation is coming from him; it is on its way! It will come from him and from no one else. He will have all the glory for it, for he alone can and will do it. And he will do it most surely, in his own time and his own way. He will save from doubt, from suffering, from slander and from distress. Though we see no sign of it yet, we are content to wait for the Lord’s will, for we have no suspicion of his love and faithfulness. He will make sure work of it before long, and we will praise him now for the mercy that is coming.

notes.term: Truly my soul waiteth upon God
notes.note: [[Ps.62.1|Psalm 62:1]]; “My soul, wait thou only upon God” ([[Ps.62.5|Psalm 62:5]]).
Waiting for his own good time.
Sulky irritability.
In the wilderness Israel moved only when the cloud of God’s presence lifted, and stayed put while it rested ([[Num.9.17-Num.9.23|Numbers 9:17–23]]).
Wait for.

modern: Am I in the light? Then you, O Lord, are my lamp. Take you away, and my joy would be gone; but as long as you are with me, I can do without the torches of time and the candles of created comfort. What a light the presence of God throws on everything! We have heard of a lighthouse that could be seen for twenty miles, but our Jehovah isn’t only a God close at hand; he is seen far off, even in the enemy’s country. O Lord, I am as happy as an angel when your love fills my heart. You are all my desire.

Am I in the dark? Then you, O Lord, will light up my darkness. Before long things will change. Matters may grow more and more dreary, and cloud may be piled on cloud; but even if it grows so dark that I can’t see my own hand, I will still see the hand of the Lord. When I can’t find any light within me, or among my friends, or in the whole world, the Lord who said, “Let there be light,” and there was light, can say the same again. He will speak me into the sunshine yet. I won’t die, but live. The day is already breaking. This sweet text shines like a morning star. I will clap my hands for joy before many hours have passed.

notes.term: Thou art my lamp, O Lord
notes.note: From David’s song of thanks after God rescued him from Saul and all his enemies ([[2Sam.22.29|2 Samuel 22:29]]).
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.

notes.term: Not only a God at hand
notes.note: “Am I a God at hand, saith the LORD, and not a God afar off?” ([[Jer.23.23|Jeremiah 23:23]]).
[[Gen.1.3|Genesis 1:3]].

notes.term: I shall not die but live
notes.note: “I shall not die, but live, and declare the works of the LORD” ([[Ps.118.17|Psalm 118:17]]).
Before.

modern: Quick work, this! The Lord hears us before we call, and often answers us just as speedily. Foreseeing our needs and our prayers, he so arranges providence that before the need actually arises he has supplied it, and before the trial attacks us he has armed us against it. This is the promptness of a God who knows everything, and we have often seen it at work. Before we dreamed of the affliction that was coming, the strong comfort that was to hold us up in it had arrived. What a prayer-answering God we have!

The second clause suggests the telephone. Though God is in heaven and we are on earth, he makes our word, like his own word, travel very swiftly. When we pray rightly, we speak into the ear of God. Our gracious Mediator presents our requests at once, and the great Father hears them and smiles on them. This is grand praying! Who wouldn’t pray a great deal, knowing that he has the ear of the King of kings? Today I will pray in faith, believing not only that I will be heard but that I am heard; not only that I will be answered but that I have the answer already. Holy Spirit, help me in this!

notes.term: Before they call, I will answer
notes.note: From God’s promise of new heavens and a new earth ([[Isa.65.24|Isaiah 65:24]]).
God’s care and control over everything that happens, providing for his people.
Promptness.
Knowing everything.
“That… we might have a strong consolation, who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us” ([[Heb.6.18|Hebrews 6:18]]).
Invented only twelve years before this book came out in 1888, so the picture was strikingly new.
The go-between who brings God and man together: “one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus” ([[1Tim.2.5|1 Timothy 2:5]]).
Requests.

notes.term: That I have the answer already
notes.note: “What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them” ([[Mark.11.24|Mark 11:24]]).

modern: In the family of grace there is discipline, and it is severe enough to make sin an evil and bitter thing. Solomon, led astray by his foreign wives, had set up other gods and deeply provoked the God of his father; so ten parts out of twelve of the kingdom were torn away and set up as a rival state. This was a heavy affliction to the house of David, and it came on that dynasty plainly from the hand of God, as the result of unholy conduct. The Lord will discipline his best-loved servants if they stop obeying his laws fully; perhaps such discipline is on us at this very hour. Let’s humbly cry, “O Lord, show me wherefore thou contendest with me.”

What a sweet saving clause that is: “but not for ever!” The punishment of sin is everlasting, but a Father’s discipline of sin in a child of God lasts only for a time. The sickness, the poverty, the depression of spirit will pass away once they have had their intended effect. Remember, we aren’t under law but under grace. The rod may sting us, but the sword won’t kill us. Our present grief is meant to bring us to repentance, so that we won’t be destroyed with the wicked.

notes.note: Offspring, descendants.

notes.term: Solomon, turned aside by his foreign wives
notes.note: In his old age Solomon’s wives turned his heart after other gods ([[1Kgs.11.1-1Kgs.11.13|1 Kings 11:1–13]]).

notes.term: Ten parts out of twelve of the kingdom were rent away
notes.note: The prophet Ahijah tore his new cloak into twelve pieces and gave Jeroboam ten, for the ten tribes that would break away ([[1Kgs.11.29-1Kgs.11.31|1 Kings 11:29–31]]). Rent means torn.
Discipline, correct.

notes.term: Show me wherefore thou contendest with me
notes.note: “Shew me wherefore thou contendest with me” ([[Job.10.2|Job 10:2]]): show me why you are fighting against me.

notes.term: Not under law, but under grace

notes.note: God’s discipline, the way a father corrects a child.

notes.term: That we may not be destroyed with the wicked
notes.note: “We are chastened of the Lord, that we should not be condemned with the world” ([[1Cor.11.32|1 Corinthians 11:32]]).

modern: Not every believer has yet learned to pray in Christ’s name. To ask not only for his sake but in his name, as authorized by him, is a high kind of prayer. We wouldn’t dare ask for some things in that blessed name, for it would be a wretched misuse of it; but when the request is so clearly right that we dare put Jesus’ name to it, then it must be granted.

Prayer is all the surer to succeed because it is for the Father’s glory through the Son. It glorifies his truth, his faithfulness, his power, his grace. Granting prayer offered in the name of Jesus shows the Father’s love for him and the honor he has put on him. The glory of Jesus and of the Father are so bound up together that the grace that magnifies the one magnifies the other. The channel is made famous by the fullness of the fountain, and the fountain is honored by the channel it flows through. If the answering of our prayers would dishonor our Lord, we wouldn’t pray; but since he is glorified in it, we will pray without ceasing in that dear name in which God and his people share a fellowship of delight.

notes.term: Whatsoever ye shall ask in my name
notes.note: Jesus to his disciples the night before his death ([[John.14.13-John.14.14|John 14:13–14]]).
Treating something holy with disrespect.
A request.
[[1Thess.5.17|1 Thessalonians 5:17]].

modern: Here is the way of mercy for a guilty, repenting sinner. He must stop the habit of covering up sin. People try to do this by lying, which denies sin; by hypocrisy, which hides it; by boasting, which excuses it; and by a loud profession of faith, which tries to make up for it.

The sinner’s business is to confess and forsake. The two must go together. Confession must be made honestly to the Lord himself, and it must include admitting the wrong, feeling its evil and hating it. We mustn’t throw the blame on others, or blame our circumstances, or plead natural weakness. We must make a clean breast of it and plead guilty to the charge. There can be no mercy until this is done.

Furthermore, we must give up the evil. Having admitted our fault, we must reject any present or future intention of staying in it. We can’t stay in rebellion and still live with the King’s Majesty. The habit of evil must be dropped, together with all the places, companions, pursuits and books that might lead us astray. Not for confessing, nor for reforming, but in connection with them, we find pardon by faith in the blood of Jesus.

notes.term: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper
notes.note: [[Prov.28.13|Proverbs 28:13]].
Publicly claiming to be a Christian. A “dead profession” is the claim with no faith behind it.
Make up for a wrong.
Hatred, disgust.

notes.term: Make a clean breast of it
notes.note: Confess everything.
A formal charge in court.
Given up, left.

modern: Horses and chariots and a great army surrounded the prophet in Dothan. His young servant was alarmed. How could they escape from such a body of armed men? But the prophet had eyes his servant didn’t have, and he could see a greater army, with far better weapons, guarding him from all harm. Horses of fire are mightier than horses of flesh, and chariots of fire are far better than chariots of iron.

It is just the same at this hour. The enemies of truth are many, influential, learned and crafty, and the truth suffers at their hands; and yet the man of God has no reason for alarm. Forces seen and unseen, of the most powerful kind, are on the side of righteousness. God has armies in ambush that will show themselves in the hour of need. The forces on the side of the good and the true far outweigh the powers of evil. So let’s keep our spirits up, and walk with the step of people who have a cheering secret that has lifted them above all fear. We are on the winning side. The battle may be sharp, but we know how it will end. Faith, with God on her side, is in a clear majority: “They that be with us are more than they that be with them.”

notes.term: They that be with us are more than they that be with them
notes.note: Elisha to his frightened servant when the Syrian army surrounded Dothan. God opened the young man’s eyes, “and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha” ([[2Kgs.6.15-2Kgs.6.17|2 Kings 6:15–17]]).
An army.
Fear, alarm.
Forces; powers at work.

modern: We need our God; he is to be had for the seeking, and he won’t refuse himself to any one of us if we seek his face personally. It doesn’t say, if you deserve him or buy his favor, but simply if you “seek” him. Those who already know the Lord must keep seeking his face by prayer, by diligent service and by holy gratitude; he won’t refuse his favor and fellowship to them. Those who haven’t yet known him so as to find rest for their souls should start seeking at once, and never stop until they find him as their Savior, their Friend, their Father and their God.

What strong assurance this promise gives the seeker! “He that seeketh findeth.” You, yes, you, will find your God if you seek him. When you find him, you have found life, pardon, holiness, protection and glory. Won’t you seek, and keep on seeking, since you won’t seek in vain? Dear friend, seek the Lord at once. Here is the place, and now is the time. Bend that stiff knee; yes, bend that stiffer neck, and cry out for God, for the living God. In the name of Jesus seek cleansing and justification. You won’t be turned away. Here is David’s testimony to his son Solomon, and it is the writer’s personal witness to the reader. Believe it and act on it, for Christ’s sake.

notes.term: If thou seek him, he will be found of thee
notes.note: David’s charge to Solomon: “but if thou forsake him, he will cast thee off for ever” ([[1Chr.28.9|1 Chronicles 28:9]]).
[[Matt.7.8|Matthew 7:8]].
The lifelong work of being made holy.
Stubbornness. God called Israel “a stiffnecked people” ([[Exod.32.9|Exodus 32:9]]).
God’s declaring a sinner righteous, through faith in Christ.

modern: God’s judgments in this life can’t always be clearly seen, for in many cases the same thing happens to everyone. This is the time of testing, not of punishment or reward. Yet at times God does terrible things in righteousness, and even the careless are forced to acknowledge his hand.

Even in this life, righteousness has the kind of reward it values above all others: the smile of God, which brings a quiet conscience. Sometimes other rewards follow, for God will be in no one’s debt. But at the same time, the chief reward of the righteous lies in the life to come.

Meanwhile, on a large scale, we see the presence of the great Ruler among the nations. He smashes oppressive thrones and punishes guilty peoples. No one can study the history of the rise and fall of empires without seeing that there is a power that makes for righteousness, and that in the end brings wickedness before its court and condemns it with unsparing justice. Sin won’t go unpunished, and goodness won’t stay unrewarded. The Judge of all the earth must do right. So let’s fear before him, and stop dreading the power of the wicked.

notes.term: Verily there is a reward for the righteous
notes.note: [[Ps.58.11|Psalm 58:11]]. Verily means truly.

notes.term: One event happeneth alike to all
notes.note: “All things come alike to all: there is one event to the righteous, and to the wicked” ([[Eccl.9.2|Ecclesiastes 9:2]]).
A time of testing.
Acknowledge that God has done it.
Rewards, repayments.

notes.term: A power which makes for righteousness
notes.note: An echo of the writer Matthew Arnold, who in 1873 described God as “a power, not ourselves, that makes for righteousness.”
Sin, wickedness.

notes.term: The Judge of all the earth must do right
notes.note: “Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?” ([[Gen.18.25|Genesis 18:25]]).

modern: In this, Eliphaz spoke God’s truth. We may have as many troubles as there are working days in the week, but the God who worked on those six days will work for us until our deliverance is complete. We will rest with him, and in him, on our Sabbath. A rapid succession of trials is one of the hardest tests of faith. Before we have recovered from one blow, another follows, and another, until we are staggered. Still, the equally quick succession of deliverances is wonderfully cheering. New songs ring out on the anvil under the hammer of affliction, until in the spiritual world we see the real thing that “the Harmonious Blacksmith” pictures. Our confidence is that when the Lord makes our trials six, six they will be, and no more.

It may be that we get no day of rest, for seven troubles come on us. What then? “In seven there shall no evil touch thee.” Evil may roar at us, but it will be kept at more than arm’s length and won’t even touch us. Its hot breath may distress us, but it can’t lay its little finger on us.
With our belts fastened around us, we will meet the six or the seven troubles, and leave fear to those who have no Father, no Savior and no Sanctifier.

notes.term: He shall deliver thee in six troubles
notes.note: Words of Eliphaz, one of Job’s three friends ([[Job.5.19|Job 5:19]]). God later rebuked the friends, but this saying is true.
The day of rest, after God’s six days of creation.
The real thing that a picture or type points to.
The popular name for a set of keyboard variations by Handel, said to have been inspired by a blacksmith’s ringing anvil.

notes.term: In seven there shall be no evil touch thee
notes.note: This edition misprints the verse, which reads “in seven there shall no evil touch thee.”

notes.term: With our loins girt about us
notes.note: With our long robes tucked into our belts, ready for action ([[Luke.12.35|Luke 12:35]]).
The one who makes us holy: the Holy Spirit.

modern: A moment under our Father’s anger seems very long, and yet it is only a moment after all. If we grieve his Spirit, we can’t expect his smile; but he is a God ready to pardon, and he soon puts aside all memory of our faults. When we faint and are ready to die because of his frown, his favor puts new life into us.

This verse has another very short note in it, like a sixteenth note in music. Our night of weeping soon turns into a day of joy. Shortness is the mark of mercy when believers are being disciplined. The Lord doesn’t like using the rod on his chosen ones. He gives a blow or two, and it is all over; yes, and the life and joy that follow the anger and weeping more than make up for the healthful sorrow.

Come, my heart, begin your hallelujahs! Don’t weep all through the night, but wipe your eyes in expectation of the morning. These tears are dews that will do us as much good as tomorrow’s sunbeams. Tears clear the eyes to see God in his grace, and make the sight of his favor more precious. A night of sorrow supplies the shadows in the picture that make the highlights stand out clearly. All is well.

notes.term: Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning

notes.note: “And grieve not the holy Spirit of God” ([[Eph.4.30|Ephesians 4:30]]).
“But thou art a God ready to pardon, gracious and merciful” ([[Neh.9.17|Nehemiah 9:17]]).
A sixteenth note: a very short note in music.
Discipline, correction.
God’s discipline, the way a father corrects a child.
Healthful; doing good.
Tomorrow.

modern: Wicked men will be angry. We must bear their anger as the badge of our calling, the sign that we are separate from them: if we were of the world, the world would love its own. Our comfort is that the wrath of man will be made to turn to the glory of God. When the wicked crucified the Son of God in their anger, they were unknowingly fulfilling God’s purpose, and in a thousand cases the willfulness of the ungodly is doing the same. They think they are free, but like convicts in chains they are unconsciously carrying out the decrees of the Almighty.

The schemes of the wicked are turned by God to their own defeat. They act in a way that destroys themselves and thwart their own plots. Nothing will come of their anger that can do us real harm. When they burned the martyrs, the smoke that blew from the stake sickened people of Roman Catholicism more than anything else.

Meanwhile, the Lord has a muzzle and a chain for bears. He holds back the more furious wrath of the enemy. He is like a miller who holds back most of the water in the stream, and uses what he does let through to turn his wheel. Let’s not sigh, but sing. All is well, however hard the wind blows.

notes.term: Surely the wrath of man shall praise thee
If we were of the world, the world would love its own
notes.note: “If ye were of the world, the world would love his own” ([[John.15.19|John 15:19]]).
Turn out, contribute.
“Him, being delivered by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God, ye have taken, and by wicked hands have crucified and slain” ([[Acts.2.23|Acts 2:23]]).
Turned by God’s control to a different end.
Nearly three hundred Protestants were burned at the stake in England under Queen Mary I (1555–1558), which turned many people against her church.
Spurgeon’s word, common among Protestants of his day, for Roman Catholicism.

modern: Wisdom loves those who love her and seeks those who seek her. Whoever seeks to be wise is already wise, and whoever seeks wisdom diligently has almost found her. What is true of wisdom in general is especially true of wisdom embodied in our Lord Jesus. Him we are to love and to seek, and in return we will enjoy his love and find him.

Our business is to seek Jesus early in life. Happy are the young whose morning is spent with Jesus! It is never too soon to seek the Lord Jesus. Early seekers are sure finders. We should seek him early by diligence. Thriving tradesmen are early risers, and thriving saints seek Jesus eagerly. Those who find Jesus to their enrichment give their hearts to seeking him. We must seek him first, and so earliest. Jesus above everything! Jesus first, and nothing else even as a poor second.

The blessing is that he will be found. He reveals himself more and more clearly to our search. He gives himself up more fully to our fellowship. Happy are those who seek the One who, once he is found, stays with them forever, a treasure growing more precious to their hearts and minds.
Lord Jesus, I have found you; be found by me to a joy and satisfaction beyond words.

notes.term: I love them that love me
notes.note: Wisdom speaking in the book of Proverbs ([[Prov.8.17|Proverbs 8:17]]), whom Christians have long seen as a picture of Christ.

notes.term: Wisdom embodied in our Lord Jesus
notes.note: “Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God” ([[1Cor.1.24|1 Corinthians 1:24]]).
Here both early in life and early in the day: eagerly, before anything else.

modern: For the worldly wise this verse is a threat, but for the simple believer it is a promise. Those who claim to be learned are forever trying to bring the humble believer’s faith to nothing, but they fail. Their arguments break down, their theories collapse under their own weight, and their carefully laid plots expose themselves before they can succeed. The old gospel isn’t dead yet, and won’t be while the Lord lives. If it could have been wiped out, it would have vanished from the earth long ago.

We can’t destroy the wisdom of the wise, and we needn’t try, for the work is in far better hands. The Lord himself says, “I will,” and he never decides anything in vain. Twice in this verse he declares his purpose, and we can rest assured he won’t turn aside from it.

What clean work the Lord makes of philosophy and “modern thought” when he sets his hand to it! He brings the fine appearance down to nothing; he utterly destroys the wood, hay and stubble. It is written that it will be so, and so it will be. Lord, make short work of it. Amen, and Amen.

notes.term: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise
notes.note: Paul quoting [[Isa.29.14|Isaiah 29:14]] in [[1Cor.1.19|1 Corinthians 1:19]].
Here, the clever and shrewd.
The new liberal theology of Spurgeon’s last years, which doubted the Bible and the atonement. He fought it in the “Downgrade Controversy” of 1887–88; this book came out in 1888.
Work that won’t survive God’s fire ([[1Cor.3.12-1Cor.3.13|1 Corinthians 3:12–13]]).

modern: Under God’s shepherding, the saints are fed to the full. Theirs isn’t a windy, unsatisfying dish of mere human “thought”; the Lord feeds them on the solid, substantial truth of divine revelation. There is real nourishment for the soul in Scripture brought home to the heart by the Holy Spirit. Jesus himself is the true, life-sustaining Food of believers. Here our Great Shepherd promises that he will give us this sacred nourishment himself. If our earthly shepherd is empty-handed on the Lord’s Day, the Lord isn’t.

When the mind is filled with holy truth, it rests. Those whom Jehovah feeds are at peace. No dog will worry them, no wolf will devour them, no restless urges will disturb them. They will lie down and digest the food they have enjoyed. The doctrines of grace don’t only sustain; they comfort. In them we have the means both of being built up and of lying down. If preachers don’t give us rest, let’s look to the Lord for it.
Today, may the Lord make us feed in the pastures of the Word and lie down in them. May no foolishness and no worry, but Meditation and Peace, mark this day.

notes.note: God’s promise to shepherd his people himself, after the false shepherds failed them ([[Ezek.34.11-Ezek.34.15|Ezekiel 34:11–15]]).
Shepherding.
An empty, unsatisfying dish of food.
The minister of our church.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
Tendencies, urges.
The teachings that salvation is God’s work from start to finish: his choosing, Christ’s death for his people, the Spirit’s call, and his keeping them to the end.

modern: Some are fat and flourishing, and so they are unkind to the weak. This is a serious sin, and it causes great sorrow. That shoving with side and shoulder, that pushing of the sick with the horn, does sad harm in the gatherings of those who profess to believe. The Lord takes note of these proud and unkind acts, and he is very angry about them, for he loves the weak.

Is the reader one of the despised? Is he a mourner in Zion, singled out because of his tender conscience? Do his brothers and sisters judge him harshly? Let him not resent the way they treat him, and above all let him not push and shove back. Let him leave the matter in the Lord’s hands. He is the Judge. Why should we want to take over his office? He will decide far more justly than we can. His time for judgment is best, and we needn’t be in a hurry to bring it on.

Let the hard-hearted oppressor tremble. Even if he rides roughshod over others and gets away with it for now, all his proud speeches are noted, and he must give account for every one of them before the court of the Great Judge.
Patience, my soul! Patience! The Lord knows your grief. Your Jesus has pity on you!

notes.term: I will judge between cattle and cattle
notes.note: God’s word against the strong sheep of his flock that trampled the pasture and “thrust with side and with shoulder, and pushed all the diseased with your horns” ([[Ezek.34.20-Ezek.34.22|Ezekiel 34:20–22]]). Cattle here means sheep and goats.
Serious; causing great pain.
A cause of stumbling; harm to faith.
“To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion… beauty for ashes” ([[Isa.61.3|Isaiah 61:3]]).
Trample on others, like a horse shod with spiked shoes.
Without being punished.
The court; the place where the accused stands for judgment.

modern: This has long been the motto hung on the wall of our bedroom, where we see it every day, and in many ways it has been written on our heart too. It is no small thing to be chosen by God. God’s choice makes chosen men choice men. Better to be God’s elect than to be elected by a whole nation. This privilege is so outstanding that whatever drawback comes with it, we accept it very joyfully, just as the Jew ate the bitter herbs for the sake of the Passover lamb. We choose the furnace, since God chooses us in it.

We are chosen as an afflicted people, not as a prosperous one; chosen not in the palace but in the furnace. In the furnace beauty is spoiled, fashion is destroyed, strength is melted and glory is burned up; and yet it is here that eternal love reveals its secrets and declares its choice. It has been so in our case. In times of the severest trial God has made our calling and election plain to us, and we have made it sure. Then we have chosen the Lord to be our God, and he has shown that we are certainly his chosen. So if the furnace is heated seven times hotter today, we won’t dread it, for the glorious Son of God will walk with us among the glowing coals.

notes.term: I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction
notes.note: “Behold, I have refined thee, but not with silver; I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction” ([[Isa.48.10|Isaiah 48:10]]).

notes.term: The motto fixed before our eye upon the wall of our bedroom
notes.note: Spurgeon, ill and in great pain for much of his life, kept this text on his bedroom wall.
Small, unimportant.
God’s chosen people.

notes.term: The bitter herbs for the sake of the Paschal Lamb
notes.note: At Passover the lamb was eaten “with unleavened bread; and with bitter herbs” ([[Exod.12.8|Exodus 12:8]]). Paschal means of the Passover.
“Give diligence to make your calling and election sure” ([[2Pet.1.10|2 Peter 1:10]]).
Nebuchadnezzar’s furnace, in which a fourth figure “like the Son of God” walked with Daniel’s three friends ([[Dan.3.19-Dan.3.25|Daniel 3:19–25]]).

modern: Yes, I must and will pray. What else can I do? What better can I do? Betrayed, abandoned, grieved, baffled, O my Lord, I will call on you. My Ziklag is in ashes, and men talk of stoning me; but I encourage my heart in the Lord, who will carry me through this trial as he has carried me through so many others. Jehovah will save me. I am sure he will, and I declare my faith.

The Lord, and no one else, will save me. I want no other helper, and I wouldn’t trust in an arm of flesh even if I could. I will cry to him evening and morning and noon, and I will cry to no one else, for he is all-sufficient.

How he will save me I can’t guess, but he will do it, I know. He will do it in the best and surest way, and in the largest, truest and fullest sense. Out of this trouble and all future troubles the great I AM will bring me, as surely as he lives; and when death comes, and all the mysteries of eternity follow, this will still be true: “the Lord shall save me.” This will be my song all through this autumn day. Isn’t it like a ripe apple from the tree of life? I will feed on it. How sweet it is to my taste!

notes.term: As for me, I will call upon God
notes.note: From David’s psalm about being betrayed by a close friend ([[Ps.55.12-Ps.55.16|Psalm 55:12–16]]).

notes.term: My Ziklag is in ashes, and men speak of stoning me
notes.note: When raiders burned David’s town of Ziklag and carried off the families, his own men talked of stoning him, “but David encouraged himself in the LORD his God” ([[1Sam.30.1-1Sam.30.6|1 Samuel 30:1–6]]).
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
Mere human strength ([[2Chr.32.8|2 Chronicles 32:8]]).
“Evening, and morning, and at noon, will I pray, and cry aloud: and he shall hear my voice” ([[Ps.55.17|Psalm 55:17]]).
God’s name for himself to Moses ([[Exod.3.14|Exodus 3:14]]).

modern: Oh, to have your soul under heavenly cultivation, no longer a wilderness but a garden of the Lord! Fenced off from the waste land, walled around by grace, planted by teaching, visited by love, weeded by heavenly discipline and guarded by divine power, the favored soul is made ready to bear fruit for the Lord.

But a garden can dry out for lack of water, and then all its plants droop and are ready to die. O my soul, how soon this would happen to you if the Lord left you! In the East, a garden without water soon stops being a garden at all; nothing can come to perfection, or grow, or even live. When the watering is kept up, the result is charming. Oh, to have your soul watered by the Holy Spirit *evenly*, every part of the garden having its own stream; *plentifully*, enough refreshment reaching every tree and plant, however thirsty it may be by nature; *continually*, each hour bringing not only its heat but its refreshment; *wisely*, each plant receiving just what it needs. In a garden you can tell by the green where the water flows, and you can soon see when the Spirit of God comes.
O Lord, water me today, and make me give you a full harvest, for Jesus’ sake. Amen.

notes.term: Their soul shall be as a watered garden
notes.note: “And they shall not sorrow any more at all” ([[Jer.31.12|Jeremiah 31:12]]).
“He will make her wilderness like Eden, and her desert like the garden of the LORD” ([[Isa.51.3|Isaiah 51:3]]).
For lack of water.
Green growth.

modern: This isn’t so much one promise as a collection of promises: a box of pearls. The covenant is the ark that contains everything.
These are the last words of David, but they can be mine today. Here is a sigh: things aren’t as I could wish with me and mine. There are trials, cares and sins, and they make the pillow hard.
Here is a comfort: “He hath made with me an everlasting covenant.” Jehovah has pledged himself to me and sealed the agreement with the blood of Jesus. I am bound to my God, and my God to me.

This brings a security into view, since this covenant is everlasting, well ordered and sure. There is nothing to fear from the passing of time, the failure of some forgotten detail or the natural uncertainty of things. The covenant is a rocky foundation to build on, for life or for death.
David feels satisfied: he wants nothing more for salvation or delight. He is rescued, and he is delighted. The covenant is all anyone could want.
O my soul, turn today to your Lord Jesus, whom the great Lord has given to be a covenant to the people. Take him to be your all in all.

notes.term: An everlasting covenant, ordered in all things, and sure
notes.note: From David’s last words ([[2Sam.23.1-2Sam.23.5|2 Samuel 23:1–5]]).
A collection; a whole made of many parts.
Comfort.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
A binding agreement.
Delight, enjoyment.
God’s word to his Servant: “I… will give thee for a covenant of the people” ([[Isa.42.6|Isaiah 42:6]]).
Everything. “Christ is all, and in all” ([[Col.3.11|Colossians 3:11]]).

modern: All human teaching, and indeed all human beings, will pass away like the grass of the meadow; but here we are assured that the Word of the Lord is of a very different kind, for it will last forever.
We have a divine gospel here; for what word can last forever except one spoken by the eternal God?

We have an ever-living gospel here, as full of life as when it first came from the lips of God; as strong as ever to convince and convert, to give new birth and comfort, to sustain and make holy, as it was in its first days of working wonders.

We have an unchanging gospel, which isn’t green grass today and dry hay tomorrow, but always the lasting truth of the unchanging Jehovah. Opinions change, but truth vouched for by God can no more change than the God who spoke it.

Here, then, we have a gospel to rejoice in, a word of the Lord we can lean our whole weight on. “For ever” includes life, death, judgment and eternity. Glory be to God in Christ Jesus for everlasting comfort. Feed on the word today, and all the days of your life.

notes.term: The word of the Lord endureth for ever
notes.note: “For all flesh is as grass… The grass withereth, and the flower thereof falleth away: but the word of the Lord endureth for ever” ([[1Pet.1.24-1Pet.1.25|1 Peter 1:24–25]]), quoting [[Isa.40.6-Isa.40.8|Isaiah 40:6–8]].
Give new birth: the new life God gives by his Spirit.
Make holy; set apart for God.
Unchanging.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
“Everlasting consolation and good hope through grace” ([[2Thess.2.16|2 Thessalonians 2:16]]).
